flow_and_hook_writes: The audit log records writes made through the generated API. A flow's `run: sql` step, a hooks.yaml `sql:` and a cron.yaml `sql:` job that INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE a table leave no audit row: the flow inserts its own into _benmore_audit_log (api(at:"audit.flow_writes"), with a whole flow file in flow_writes_example). `benmore check` and the check after a push warn about a flow job, a hook or a cron.yaml job that writes a table of the app and inserts none.
flow_responses: Encrypted-field masks apply to the generated API, page queries and the admin panel. A flow's SQL result is decrypted and not masked, so a flow that responds with a `SELECT *` row gives every caller it admits the encrypted columns in clear; only the `<col>_blind` blind-index value is left out of the response (api(at:"encryption.flow_results")). `benmore check` and the check after a push warn about such a response; name the columns the flow returns.
token_scopes: A scoped API token is narrowed on the generated API, and a server-rendered page that requires sign-in, like its GET /pdf/<page>, refuses it (403 `scoped_credential_page`), so a `visit_notes:read` token cannot request a chart page. A flow that declares no `permissions:` still runs as the token's account (api(at:"auth.credential_limits"), api(at:"auth.api_tokens")). Give integrations an account of their own with the role they need, and declare `permissions:` on the flows they call.
probe_sessions: `benmore probe <app> <METHOD> <path> --as <user> --reason "..."` (probe_route with `as`) and a headless-browser session as a user (browser_check, browser_batch or qa_inventory with `as`; `benmore verify` journeys with a `user:`) act as an app user without that user's second factor; each needs a stated reason, which the app's audit log keeps. The app's audit log names the platform user behind each one in a `data_delegated_session` row; the reads it makes are recorded as the end user's (workforce_reads).
account_events: Sign-ins (successful or failed) and lockouts write no audit row unless the app sets `auth.sign_in_audit: true`, which `compliance: hipaa` does not turn on: set it in a hipaa app that must show who signed in and who was refused (api(at:"audit.sign_ins")). Sign-outs, sign-ups that issue no session and the end of a support session write none either way. Changes to an account's credentials do, each in the transaction of the change: password changes and resets, MFA enrollment and removal (also when a reset or a claim removes it), backup codes issued and used, email changes, API tokens minted and revoked, sessions ended by their owner, passkey changes, a disconnected social provider, role changes and grants, support sessions and act-as (api(at:"audit.account_events")).
right_of_access_export: GET /api/_my-data exports the rows whose `user_id` is the caller (api(at:"components.my_data")). Where records about a patient are written by staff (notes, labs and prescriptions owned by a clinician and reached by the patient through member-of), the patient's export holds their profile and the rows they created themselves, not the records written about them, and a clinician's export holds the notes of their patients. A patient's right-of-access export is a flow of the app's own that selects the patient's records by the app's rule (a membership or a patient id) and names its columns.
